Day 28 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Patterns

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished journey entry

Patterns decide which inventory hosts a command or play targets, making selection logic part of the safety model.

Architecture / mental model

inventory set + host pattern → matched host set → task execution

How it works

Patterns can target groups, individual hosts, intersections, exclusions and combinations. This makes them powerful enough to describe production subsets without duplicating playbooks.

A safe pattern is one you can explain before you run it. For broad changes, list the matches first rather than discovering the set while the change is already in progress.

Patterns are especially valuable when environment groups are modeled cleanly in inventory because targeting then expresses intent instead of host-by-host maintenance.

Hands-on reference

ansible 'web:&prod' -i inventory.ini --list-hosts
ansible 'all:!db' -i inventory.ini --list-hosts

Verification

Use `--list-hosts` before the real command or play and compare the result against the exact systems you intended to change.

Field note / gotcha

Exclusion and intersection syntax is compact enough to be misread. Preview the matched set instead of trusting punctuation under pressure.

Security considerations

Treat host selection as a change-control boundary. The same task against the wrong group can become a security incident.

What I learned

Automation safety is partly about writing the task and partly about proving who will receive it.
